avoid_when: A vendor-managed-only service boundary is mandatory.
Provider portability is a dominant requirement.
The team cannot own cloud platform integration and lifecycle operations.
patterns.decision: Place the primary coding-agent control, execution, identity, policy, evidence, and observability boundaries in customer-governed AWS services.

evidence.statement: Provider-neutral architecture and deterministic constraints precede named service selection.
Amazon Bedrock provides managed, region-scoped access to frontier models with private connectivity via VPC endpoints, removing the need to operate inference infrastructure.

recommended_when: Customer-managed or hybrid execution is required.
Security controls, auditability, and operational integration outweigh fastest initial delivery.

patterns.summary: Use AWS-managed governance, execution, model access, observability, and security services as the primary coding-agent platform boundary.
patterns.title: AWS governed managed platform
tradeoffs: Delivery is usually slower than a SaaS-first launch and faster than a fully self-hosted platform.
Managed AWS services reduce infrastructure ownership but retain AWS service coupling.
Strong governance and operational integration increase platform engineering work.

avoid_when: A single managed service already satisfies the required control boundary.
Fastest initial delivery is the dominant objective.
The organization lacks capacity to maintain integration contracts across providers.
patterns.decision: Use explicit platform contracts and adapters so customers can select or replace model, execution, tool, memory, and governance implementations.

evidence.statement: Provider-neutral architecture and deterministic constraints precede named service selection.

recommended_when: Long-running or durable remote workspaces are required.
Provider portability and replaceable implementation boundaries are strategic requirements.
The platform team can own adapter contracts, conformance tests, and lifecycle management.
patterns.summary: Preserve replaceable provider boundaries through contracts and adapters around customer-selected platform services.
patterns.title: BYOP portable platform
tradeoffs: Common contracts can limit access to provider-specific features unless extensions are governed.
Durable workspaces improve continuity while expanding state, isolation, patching, and recovery responsibilities.
Portability reduces provider coupling but increases integration and conformance work.

avoid_when: Cross-provider identity, networking, telemetry, and incident operations cannot be owned.
Data transfer across the SaaS and customer boundary is prohibited.
The organization requires a single-provider support and failure domain.
patterns.decision: Keep sensitive execution, identity, policy, evidence, and telemetry in customer-governed services while using SaaS where it materially improves developer experience or delivery speed.

evidence.statement: Provider-neutral architecture and deterministic constraints precede named service selection.

recommended_when: Customer-managed or hybrid execution is required but a SaaS developer experience is acceptable.
Identity, policy, telemetry, and incident ownership can span provider boundaries.
The organization needs stronger portability than a single-provider managed stack.
patterns.summary: Combine customer-governed execution and controls with selected SaaS experience or orchestration services.
patterns.title: Hybrid governed platform
tradeoffs: Portability improves only where contracts and evidence remain provider-neutral.
Split ownership requires explicit responsibility, telemetry correlation, and failure handling.
The pattern balances experience and control at the cost of cross-provider operational complexity.

avoid_when: Fastest time to value or minimal platform operations is the primary objective.
Managed-service certifications or support obligations are mandatory.
The organization cannot sustain patching, upgrades, capacity, recovery, and incident response.
patterns.decision: Run the primary coding-agent control, execution, model, tool, evidence, and observability boundaries on customer-operated open-source infrastructure.

evidence.statement: Provider-neutral architecture and deterministic constraints precede named service selection.

Self-hosted, in-VPC or air-gapped inference keeps model traffic and data within a controlled boundary, satisfying data-residency and sovereignty constraints at the cost of operating the serving stack.

recommended_when: Customer control, sovereignty, customization, or air-gapped operation is mandatory.
Operational ownership is an accepted strategic cost.
The organization has mature Kubernetes, security, supply-chain, and SRE capabilities.
patterns.summary: Operate the coding-agent control and execution planes on customer-managed open-source infrastructure.
patterns.title: Open-source sovereign platform
tradeoffs: Maximum control and customization create the largest operational and security ownership surface.
Software license savings do not imply lower total platform cost.
Sovereignty improves only when model, telemetry, artifact, and support paths remain inside the required boundary.

avoid_when: Customer-controlled execution or strict workload sovereignty is mandatory.
Provider portability and replaceability are dominant requirements.
Required controls depend on evidence the vendor cannot expose.
patterns.decision: Use vendor-managed coding-agent services for the primary experience and execution path while governing enterprise identity, repositories, tools, data, and audit integrations.

evidence.statement: Provider-neutral architecture and deterministic constraints precede named service selection.

recommended_when: Delivery speed and low platform operating effort are dominant objectives.
Product controls, data handling, regional availability, and audit integration satisfy customer policy.
Vendor-managed or hybrid execution is acceptable.
patterns.summary: Use vendor-managed coding-agent control and execution capabilities with governed enterprise integrations.
patterns.title: Composable SaaS platform
tradeoffs: Enterprise integration remains necessary even when the core service is managed.
Exit planning, data portability, audit access, and service lifecycle must be governed explicitly.
